extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and USPTO examiners (users of the MPEP)
extracted.subtask_short: petition to make special and suspension
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural criteria for requesting and handling 'special' status (accelerated examination) and for suspension/deferral of Office action in U.S. patent applications, including required contents, fees, time limits, processing steps, and decisions by PTO officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerequisites for special status (accelerated examination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each application requesting special status must meet on its own all requirements for the new special status and submit specified materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must (C) submit a statement that a pre-examination search was made, listing field of search by class/subclass, publications, Chemical Abstracts, foreign patents, etc. (a foreign patent office search satisfies this); (D) submit one copy each of the references deemed most closely related to the claimed subject matter if not already of record; and (E) submit a detailed discussion of the references pointing out, with the particularity required by 37 CFR 1.111(b) and (c), how the claimed subject matter is patentable over the references. If the request does not meet prerequisites, applicant will be notified of defects and given one opportunity to perfect the petition; further renewals are discretionary with the Technology Center Special Program Examiner. Once granted, there is no provision to withdraw this special status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated examination procedural steps after grant
rubrics_metrics.description: When special status is granted for accelerated examination, the examiner will take up the application ahead of most others and give a complete first action covering all claims; the examiner's search is restricted to the subject matter encompassed by the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A first action rejection sets a 3-month shortened period for reply. During that period applicant is encouraged to arrange an interview; applicant or representative should deliver a copy of proposed amendment at least one working day before the interview (that paper won't become part of the file). The formal 'record' reply must be restricted to the rejections, objections, and requirements made; any amendment broadening the search field is treated as improper. The examiner will, within 1 month from receipt of applicant's formal reply, take up the application for final disposition (final action terminating with a 3-month period for reply, or notice of allowance). Examiner may use telephone for minor issues. Personal interviews after a final Office action are not permitted unless requested by the examiner; telephonic interviews may be allowed for correcting minor matters. After allowance these applications receive top priority for printing (see MPEP §1309).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special status for superconductivity inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may request 'special' status for applications involving superconductive materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To participate, applicants should request special status accompanied by a statement under 37 CFR 1.102 that the invention involves superconductive materials. Examples include inventions directed to superconductive materials themselves and to their manufacture and application. No fee is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special status for HIV/AIDS and cancer inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: The PTO will accord special status to patent applications relating to HIV/AIDS and cancer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must file a petition and the fee under 37 CFR 1.17(h) requesting special status. The petition should be accompanied by a statement explaining how the invention contributes to the diagnosis, treatment or prevention of HIV/AIDS or cancer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special status for counter-terrorism inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: The PTO will accord special status to patent applications relating to countering terrorism technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should file a petition with the petition fee under 37 CFR 1.17(h) and include a statement explaining how the invention contributes to countering terrorism. The manual provides a definition of international terrorism from 18 U.S.C. 2331 and non-limiting examples of relevant technologies (e.g., detecting/identifying explosives, aircraft sensors/security systems, vehicular barricades/disabling systems).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special status for biotechnology applications filed by small entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Small entities may request special status for biotechnology applications, subject to specified statements and fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must file a petition with the fee under 37 CFR 1.17(h) and (A) state that small entity status has been established or include a statement establishing that status; (B) state that the subject of the patent application is a major asset of the small entity; and (C) state that development of the technology will be significantly impaired if examination is delayed, including an explanation of the basis for that statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal requirements of a petition to make special
rubrics_metrics.description: Any petition to make special must meet basic formalities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition should (A) be in writing and (B) identify the application by application number and filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling and recordation of petitions to make special
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions to make special are entered into the application file and processed with specified control measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each petition, regardless of ground and nature of decision, is made of record in the file with the decision. The petition and supporting papers receive a single paper number and entry in the 'Contents'; the decision receives a separate paper number. The TC part that rules on the petition is responsible for entering the petition and decision in the file. Technical support ensures all prior papers are entered before forwarding for petition consideration. Petitions to make special are decided by the Special Program Examiner of the assigned Technology Center.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition under 37 CFR 1.103(a) — showing of good and sufficient cause
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to suspend action under 37 CFR 1.103(a) must be properly presented and supported by good and sufficient cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition must (A) be presented as a separate paper, (B) be accompanied by the petition fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(h), (C) request a specific and reasonable period of suspension not greater than 6 months, and (D) present good and sufficient reasons why the suspension is necessary. Petitions to suspend to allow time to submit an IDS will be denied as failing to present good and sufficient reasons (37 CFR 1.97 provides recourse). Mere inclusion of a request to delay in a transmittal letter is insufficient to avoid immediate action; consider a deferral under 37 CFR 1.103(d) where appropriate. Examiner notes: maximum period is 6 months; only the Technology Center Director can grant second or subsequent suspensions (MPEP §1003).

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for suspension under 37 CFR 1.103(b) or (c) (CPA/RCE) — filing-time requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests to suspend action under 37 CFR 1.103(b) or (c) are limited to suspensions filed at the time of filing a CPA or RCE and have special requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request must be filed at the time of filing the CPA or RCE (use the check box on PTO/SB/29 or PTO/SB/30 or a separate paper). If filed with an RCE, the RCE must comply with 37 CFR 1.114 (i.e., be accompanied by a submission and the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(e)); payment of the RCE filing fee may not be deferred. If filed with a CPA, a filing date must be assigned to the CPA. The request should specify the period of suspension in whole months (maximum 3 months). If no period or an excessive period specified, the Office will assume 3 months. The request must include the processing fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of missing parts for CPA when suspension requested
rubrics_metrics.description: If a filing date is accorded to a CPA, a suspension request will be processed even if the CPA lacks a filing fee, but the missing-part processing continues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant will receive notice and have 2 months from that notification to pay the CPA filing fee and surcharge set forth in 37 CFR 1.16(e) to avoid abandonment. The suspension starts on the filing date of the CPA and suspends a first Office action by the examiner but does not affect processing for the missing part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of improper RCE/CPA or improper suspension request
rubrics_metrics.description: Improper filings or improper suspension requests will not produce a suspension and have specified handling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the CPA or RCE is improper (no filing date, missing submission or fee), the Office will not recognize the suspension request and will send a Notice of Improper CPA Filing or Notice of Improper Request for Continued Examination. Time periods from previous Office communications continue to run. If the CPA/RCE is properly filed but the suspension request is improper (untimely or lacking processing fee), action will not be suspended, the Office will process the CPA/RCE and place the application on the examiner's docket, and the examiner will notify applicant of denial in the next Office communication using form paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper request for suspension processing and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: When a CPA/RCE and suspension request are proper, the Office processes the request and places the application in suspension status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical support will process the CPA/RCE and suspension request, send a notification of approval to applicant, and place the application in suspension status until the suspension period ends. The suspension acts to suspend a first Office action by the examiner; once expired the application is placed on the examiner's docket for further prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for deferral of examination under 37 CFR 1.103(d) — basic requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may request a deferral of examination for new applications under 37 CFR 1.103(d) for up to three years from the earliest filing date for which benefit is claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request must be filed before the Office issues an Office action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance. Form PTO/SB/37 may be used. The request must include a period of suspension in whole months not extending beyond three years from the earliest effective filing date, the publication fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.18(d), and the processing fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(i). If the request includes no period or a period beyond the maximum, the Office will assume the maximum is requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions that must be met to grant deferral under 1.103(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will not grant deferral of examination unless specific conditions relating to application type, filing date, publication status, and Office actions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions include: (A) the application must be an original utility or plant application filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b) or a national-stage application after compliance with 1.494 or 1.495 (design, reissue, or CPA under 1.53(d) are ineligible); (B) the application must be filed on or after Nov 29, 2000 (or if filed before that date the applicant must submit a request for voluntary publication under 1.221, pay voluntary publication fee 1.17(i), submit a copy compliant with EFS requirements, and include the confirmation number); (C) the applicant has not filed a nonpublication request under 1.213(a) (or must rescind such request under 1.213(b)); (D) the application must be in condition for publication as provided in 1.211(c); and (E) the Office must not have issued an Office action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151.

rubrics_metrics.name: Granting/denying deferral — supervisory approval and notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Supervisory patent examiner approval is required to grant a deferral of examination and form paragraphs are provided to notify applicants of grant or denial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the request is improper, form paragraph ¶7.56.02 can be used to deny the request with reasons (examples provided). If proper, supervisory approval is required and ¶7.54.01 may be used to notify applicant that deferral was approved, specifying filing date and number of months for the deferral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of suspension of action
rubrics_metrics.description: Suspension may be terminated prior to the end of the suspension period upon request, and the termination is effective when the Office official acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request for termination will be effective when an appropriate Office official acts; if the suspension has not expired when the Office acts, the Office will terminate the suspension and place the application on the examiner's docket. An acknowledgment should be sent to applicant using the prescribed form paragraph ¶7.54.02. Examiner notes advise how to populate form paragraph fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of action on initiative of the Office (37 CFR 1.103(e),(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may suspend action on its own initiative under specified rules; initial suspensions may be granted by examiners, but subsequent suspensions require higher approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under 37 CFR 1.103(e) the Office will notify applicant if it suspends action on its own initiative. An examiner may grant an initial suspension on his/her own initiative for a maximum period of 6 months; any second or subsequent suspension is decided by the Technology Center Director (MPEP §1003). Suspension under 37 CFR 1.103(f) (public safety or defense) is decided by the TC Director of work group 3640. Form paragraphs (e.g., ¶7.52 'Suspension of Action, Awaiting New Reference' and ¶7.53 'Suspension of Action, Possible Interference') are provided. Examiner notes reiterate maximum period and approval requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overlapping applications (same applicant or same assignee) — handling during inter partes proceedings and interferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should not consider ex parte questions pending before the Office in inter partes proceedings involving the same applicant; related applications with overlapping claims and interference issues have special handling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where one application with overlapping claims is in an interference, better practice is to reject claims in the related application over the interference counts and suspend prosecution pending final determination of priority. If applicant wishes to prosecute the outside application and presents good reasons, prosecution may be continued. Cases and authorities cited (Ex parte Jones, Ex parte McCormick, In re Seebach, In re Hammell) provide precedent; see MPEP §804.03 for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory period for reply and abandonment rules (37 CFR 1.135)
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to reply within the time provided under 37 CFR 1.134 and 1.136 causes abandonment; statutory and practice rules define maximum reply periods and circumstances for relief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.135(a) – application becomes abandoned if applicant fails to reply within the provided time. 1.135(b) – prosecution to save an application from abandonment must include a complete and proper reply; admission or refusal to admit amendments after final rejection or amendments not responsive to the last action will not save the application. 1.135(c) – when reply is a bona fide attempt and substantially complete except for an inadvertent omission, the applicant may be given a new time period to supply the omission. Maximum statutory period for reply is 6 months (35 U.S.C. 133); shortened periods are generally used. The MPEP explains changes in practice regarding prior non-statutory time limits for supplying omissions.
